topic: Fine-tune on AMD: Unsloth Docker in three moves.
title: Fine-tune on AMD: the ROCm Docker image
description: Fine-tune LLMs on an AMD Radeon with Unsloth's unsloth-rocm Docker image, no NVIDIA card and no hand-pinned ROCm stack required. Unsloth publishes AMD floors: Qwen3.5 fine-tunes in 3GB of VRAM and Gemma 4 in 8GB, with PyTorch built for ROCm, bitsandbytes, triton-rocm, TRL, PEFT and diffusers pre-installed. You'll learn the docker run command with /dev/kfd and /dev/dri, the built-in smoke test, and the honest limits: RDNA1 is inference-only, multi-GPU is Linux-only, and this is a training image for now. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_text: AMD boxes don't need CUDA anymore.

narration_full: AMD boxes don't need a CUDA card anymore. Every tutorial said it: fine-tuning needs a big NVIDIA card, and your Radeon is for games. Unsloth's floor says Qwen three point five fine-tunes in three gigabytes of VRAM, the memory on your card. What is true now: Unsloth ships a Docker image, a ready-to-run package holding an app plus every dependency. The unsloth-rocm image carries the whole training stack. Gemma four fine-tunes in eight gigabytes of VRAM, a floor an aging Radeon clears. The image is the meal kit, the matched stack in one box. The manual route was grocery shopping. You hunted a PyTorch wheel that matched your ROCm version, AMD's open GPU compute platform. Then a pre-release bitsandbytes wheel for the four-bit fix. One pull replaces the trip. The run command passes AMD's kernel device nodes instead of NVIDIA's GPU flag. Your card reaches Docker through the kernel driver, not a container toolkit. A built-in smoke test runs a real training pass and fails loudly if the GPU is unusable. The method is QLoRA: load the model quantized, compressed to use less memory, and train small adapter weights on top. That is what cuts VRAM to the floor. Unsloth claims seventy percent less memory use with no accuracy loss. The honest catch: their own measured gain lands short of the headline claim. It trains RDNA two, the Radeon architecture of recent generations, and newer. Older RDNA one cards get Vulkan inference only, and the Steam Deck's chip is refused. Multi-GPU training stays Linux-only. The myth still wins here: this is a training image. The web UI, JupyterLab, and the prebuilt inference servers stay CUDA-only for now, so some shopping remains. Your AMD box is a fine-tuning rig tonight. You install Docker, you pull unsloth-rocm, you train.

analogy.vehicle: Frozen meal kit vs grocery shopping
analogy.mapping: The unsloth-rocm Docker image is the pre-portioned kit, the whole matched training stack in one box, while the manual route is shopping for each ingredient, matching a PyTorch wheel to a ROCm version and hunting a pre-release bitsandbytes wheel, hoping the versions combine into dinner.
analogy.limit: The kit does not carry the web UI or the inference extras, so some shopping remains.
